items.body_md:
*In re Sleep Number Corporation, et al.*, Case No. 26-11399 (KYP), U.S. Bankruptcy Court, S.D.N.Y. (Hon. Kyu Young Paek). Today's delta is modest in volume but not in significance: the single most consequential filing from the August 6 cluster — Dkt. 526, the Second Stipulation With Prepetition Loan Agent Extending Committee Challenge Deadline Pursuant To Final DIP Financing Order — was flagged in yesterday's briefing as unverified and remains so from available public sources. Its substance now warrants direct attention. Under a standard final DIP order, the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors receives a defined window to investigate and, if warranted, challenge the validity, priority, or extent of prepetition secured liens — here, the liens securing the $260 million DIP facility documented as the Fourteenth Amendment to the existing Amended and Restated Credit and Security Agreement, with U.S. Bank National Association as administrative agent (__[Bondoro](https://bondoro.com/sleep-number/)__). A second stipulation extending that deadline, agreed between the Committee and the prepetition loan agent, signals that the investigation is live and that the Committee has not yet exhausted its review — or has identified issues that require more time to develop. For unsecured creditors, any successful challenge to lien validity or scope is the clearest path to enlarging the unencumbered asset pool available for general distribution; each extension of the challenge deadline preserves that optionality. The specific new deadline set by Dkt. 526 is not summarized in available public sources and should be confirmed against the docket directly.

The Third Designation Rights Period Rejection Notice (Dkt. 525) and the related A&G Realty Partners retention order (Dkt. 522) were covered yesterday; no new public reporting has moved on either entry since. The Deloitte & Touche LLP independent auditor application (Dkt. 520, effective July 14, 2026) similarly requires no additional treatment today — it is an administrative professional-retention filing, not a dispositive creditor event — though its July 14 effective date, nearly three weeks after the petition date of June 12, 2026, is worth noting as a data point on the pace at which post-sale audit infrastructure is being assembled. 
The § 341 meeting of creditors was held by Zoom conference on July 24, 2026
, and the estate is now deep in the post-sale administrative phase; professional retention and fee disclosure filings will continue to accumulate through the bar date period. The fee statements filed August 5 — Davis Polk's first monthly statement at Dkt. 516 and Vinson & Elkins' first monthly statement at Dkt. 517, both covering June 12 through June 30, 2026 — remain without publicly summarized dollar figures. Creditors focused on administrative expense accrual should pull both filings directly; the Special Investigation Committee's Vinson & Elkins engagement in particular bears watching as fee statements accumulate, since the pace of billing reflects the pace of the underlying potential-claims review.

The next concrete milestones are August 20, 2026 (adjourned case conference at 10:00 a.m. in Courtroom 610, New York, at which the Third Designation Rights Period Rejection Notice objection deadline also falls), and 
September 10, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. (ET), the General Claims Bar Date
 — now 34 days out. Any creditor that has not yet filed a proof of claim should treat August 20 as the practical last-review date before the bar date window closes.
